title: Discovering Physically Interpretable Mathematical Expression for Predicting CO2 Adsorption in Metal-Organic Frameworks via Machine Learning-Symbolic Regression
authors: Yimin Shao, Shengluo Ma, Shenghong Ju, Yijun Shi, Wei Li
abstract: This work presents a machine learning-symbolic regression (ML-SR) strategy to develop a physically interpretable formula for predicting low pressure CO2 adsorption capacity in hypothetical metal-organic frameworks (hMOFs). Four ML models were trained on a small dataset of 1,000 samples, and five key descriptors-largest cavity diameter, pore limiting diameter, void fraction, gravimetric surface area, and number of hydrogen atoms-were identified through SHAP and feature importance analyses. Symbolic regression was then employed to derive a concise adsorption formula, Q=aA, where a represents an adsorption baseline (mmol/g) and A is a dimensionless adsorption number incorporating four structural descriptors. We interpret A as the ratio between an adsorption binding force and a diffusion driving force, revealing how pore topology and surface chemistry jointly influence adsorption. Validation against a comprehensive dataset of 137,652 hMOFs demonstrates that this formula achieves over 70% prediction accuracy for 62,448 structures, confirming strong applicability within defined structural and operational ranges. Unlike conventional black box ML models, the proposed physics-guided expression enables efficient prediction and provides clearer insight into adsorption mechanisms.
summary: This work pioneers the use of Machine Learning-Symbolic Regression (ML-SR) to predict CO2 adsorption in MOFs. By deriving a simple, physically interpretable formula rather than relying on a black box model, it provides deep insight into how pore topology and surface chemistry govern gas uptake. This methodology offers a powerful template for creating predictive models across various condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a physically interpretable mathematical formula for predicting low-pressure CO2 adsorption capacity in hypothetical Metal-Organic Frameworks (hMOFs). This aims to move beyond 'black box' machine learning predictions.
main_result: A concise, physics-guided formula of the form Q=aA was derived and validated against a large dataset, achieving over 70% prediction accuracy for thousands of structures. The dimensionless term A is interpreted as the ratio between an adsorption binding force and a diffusion driving force.
method: The study employs a Machine Learning–Symbolic Regression (ML-SR) strategy. After training multiple ML models (e.g., XGBoost), feature importance analysis guides symbolic regression to derive explicit, interpretable mathematical equations.
model_or_system: The physical system studied is Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs). The prediction targets the CO2 adsorption capacity at low pressures, using structural descriptors like pore size, surface area, and void fraction as inputs.
key_observables: CO2 adsorption capacity (Q in mmol/g), dimensionless adsorption number (A), Prediction Accuracy ($R^2$, AER).
important_parameters: Low pressure regime ($\le 1$ bar), key structural descriptors (void fraction, pore limiting diameter, etc.).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the complex physical process of gas adsorption can be accurately modeled by a simple, underlying mathematical relationship discoverable through symbolic regression.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the workflow from ML training to SHAP analysis and final SR validation. Tables compare empirical equation predictions against experimental data for various MOFs.
paper_structure: The paper follows a progression: first, establishing the need for interpretable models; second, applying standard ML techniques (training/feature importance); third, using symbolic regression constrained by physical units to derive candidate formulas; and finally, validating these derived formulas on large datasets.
